dataset: Pipe insulation jackets, facings, vapor retarders and vapor-retarder coatings: verified data for jacket compatibility, temperature limits and vapor-retarder notes

units.thickness: mil = 0.001 in; metal gauges in inches
units.permeance: perms (grains/hr·ft²·in Hg) unless the source prints another unit; perm-in = permeability of a material, not permeance

conventions.unverified: The literal string 'unverified' means no fetched primary source stated the value. Nothing was guessed, averaged, converted or filled from memory. No permeance was computed from a permeability.
conventions.src: Every fact carries 'src', a list of ids in the top-level 'sources' array. One shared sources array is used here because several documents (e.g. the JM Metal Jacketing Install Guide) cover more than one item.
conventions.quotes: 'quote' strings are verbatim from the source text (pdftotext output or page text). Line breaks and hyphenation splits were joined; nothing else was changed. A broken 'ti' ligature in one Polyguard PDF was restored and this is noted where it applies.
conventions.service_vs_operating: Jacket and coating temperature limits apply to the jacket or coated surface, not to the pipe operating temperature, unless the quote says otherwise. JM's Saranex sheets define it explicitly (see vapor_retarders: Saranex footnote).
conventions.typical_values: Manufacturer values are typical, subject to change without notice. Confirm against the current sheet before using a number in a submittal.

method: Manufacturer PDFs were downloaded with curl and read with pdftotext (raw and -layout). ASTM scope text comes from the public store.astm.org pages; full ASTM tables (e.g. C1136 per-type permeance) are paywalled and not reproduced. Product pages were read from their HTML. The H.B. Fuller product site (hbfullerproducts.com) returned an AWS WAF challenge to every request, so the Foster 30-65 sheet was taken from H.B. Fuller's own fosterproducts.com domain (latest revision found there: R1119).

discrepancies_between_products: Insert-layer threshold on hot fittings: JM data sheet says insulation 'greater than 1½”' (JM catalog says '1½ inches or greater'); Proto says 'greater than 1”'. Both use 250°F as the temperature trigger. JM also uses 45°F as the cold trigger.
Minimum temperature: Proto prints -20°F (exposed surface). JM prints no minimum for the PVC (only Z-Tape's 0°F to +150°F installed range).

Outdoor PVC: JM recommends 30 mil Cut & Curled (white only) outdoors. Proto requires 0.030 in minimum and 0.040 in over 15 in O.D., white only, with caulked joints and 8 in slip joints every 25 ft. ASTM C1917 itself excludes direct-sunlight exposure and defers to the manufacturer.
Permeance: Proto publishes E96 values by thickness; JM publishes none.
JM Zeston 300 data sheet prints CT sizes 'from 5/8" through 68" (16 mm through 156 mm)'; 156 mm is about 6-1/8 in, so '68"' looks like a typo. Not used.

astm_specs.designation: ASTM C1729-26 (active; prior C1729-21 and earlier)
astm_specs.title: Standard Specification for Aluminum Jacketing for Insulation
scope_quotes: 1.1 This specification covers aluminum jacketing for thermal and acoustical insulation operating at either above or below ambient temperatures and in both indoor and outdoor locations. It does not cover insulation jacketing made from other materials such as mastics, fiber reinforced plastic, PVC, or stainless steel nor does it cover the details of thermal or acoustical insulation systems.
1.2 This specification provides physical requirements for aluminum jacketing for thermal and acoustical insulation. Guide C1423 provides guidance in selecting jacketing materials and their safe use.
1.3 This is a material specification and does not imply any performance of the installed system using the materials specified herein.
astm_specs.classification_quote: Classification of aluminum jacketing is based on three factors: outer surface treatment and emittance, alloy and temper per Specification B209, and moisture retarder.
astm_specs.classification_quote_src_note: From the C1729-21 store-page abstract; the C1729-26 abstract does not repeat this sentence.
astm_specs.test_methods_quote: Test methods cover total hemispherical emittance, surface burning characteristics, metal sheet thickness, pinholes in moisture retarder, pencil hardness, and water vapor transmission rate of the moisture retarder.
astm_specs.temperature_statement: Only 'above or below ambient temperatures and in both indoor and outdoor locations'. No numeric temperature limit on the public page.
astm_specs.type_grade_class_definitions: unverified (paywalled). See JM's property-to-classification pairings below.

PFMB Film is colored a light blue to distinguish it from other film types

not_a_vapor_retarder.quote: Aluminum or stainless steel protective jacketing shall not be considered a vapor retarder.

galvanic_and_corrosion.quote: JM recommends the use of PFMB on all aluminum jacketing to help prevent pitting, crevice, and galvanic corrosion of the interior surface of the metal jacketing and the insulated pipe, tank, or equipment.

Polyfilm is very important in all applications but is essential in applications in which the metal jacketing comes in contact with dissimilar metals, e.g. wire mesh that is used around mineral wool blankets or tie wire used to hold pipe sections in place.
ASJ that is wet most of the time may greatly increase the chance of the aluminum jacketing corroding within one to five years.
Smooth finish is less susceptible to poultice/crevice corrosion than stucco embossed.
Where maximum resistance to corrosion is required, JM stainless steel jacketing (T304 or T316) should be used.

rooftop_cold_recommendation.text: Ammonia/chilled-water rooftop piping: .016 or .020 in smooth white-painted aluminum with polyfilm, a paperless vapor retarder jacket (e.g. Saranex) beneath, longitudinal joints at 3 o'clock, 1/2 in x .020 in 300-series stainless bands on 12 in centers.

limitations.quote: For applications where a maximum resistance to fire is required, stainless steel jacketing should be used

limitations.text: Roll jacketing for pipe and for vertical tanks up to 8 ft O.D. Above 8 ft, use deep corrugated sheet.

fastening.quote: Neatly secure straight sections of jacketing with bands and seals with a maximum spacing of 12 in (305 mm) on center. Secure end joints with bands and seals centered directly over joint. Do not use screws, staples, or other fasteners that can penetrate the vapor retarder.
When used on above ambient systems, screws shall be installed at a maximum spacing of 8” on center on the longitudinal joint of straight pipe jacketing sections.
Screws shall be installed at a maximum spacing of 3” on center on the longitudinal joint of elbow covers.
In applications where the pipe is cold (below ambient temperature), banding should be used, unless unavoidable.

fastening.text: Where screws are unavoidable on cold work (heads, valves, nozzles, tees), JM says to install a sacrificial layer of elastomeric foam over the vapor retarder and recommends #8 x 1/2 in stainless screws.

Banding: stainless 0.020 in, T304/T316 annealed; 1/2 or 3/4 in wide below 16 in O.D., 3/4 in at 16 in O.D. and up. Aluminum banding (0.020 in, 3105/3003) only when all of the following hold: aluminum jacketing and covers; jacket no thicker than the band; no excessive forces; non-corrosive environment; insulation O.D. ≤8 in; non-rigid insulation.
